title: Born 1900 in the Third Ward: social clubs, halls and Bunk Johnson
summary: Watkins gives his birth date and describes the Third Ward pleasure clubs, parades, dance halls and hearing Bunk Johnson as a child.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: October 24th. I was born in 1900, Chattery Hospital. And lived in the Third Ward quite a few years. Oh. Well, I've taken music inspiration from the different jazz brass bands they had around that ward. Not that particular ward. But several wards all had social and pleasure clubs. You had the Magnorias, you had the Pickles, you had the Taminets, and several other aid and pleasure clubs. And all during the summer months, each one of them would have a parade. They'd have a parade on Sunday afternoons and balls on Monday nights. Yeah. Well, in them days you had Kenny's Hall, which was a dance hall. And you had the old Masonic Hall, where it was at Rampart and the corner of Pedita. And Kenny's Hall was on Pedita between Liberty and Franklin. Well, I can't use the expression that they used to call these old Halls, but anyhow. My guard mother used to take me there when I was a kid.

And them days, Bunk Johnson was playing there. That was on Saturday nights. Every Saturday night they had a dance sometime, they'd have them on Sunday nights. Remember who was with Bunk in that family? No, because I was too small. See, I was too small at that time to remember who was playing with them.
But just the sixth grade was...

Well, anyway, I think it was Bunk Johnson. And, well, Lurie was small at that time, too. We used to play together, and most of the time Lurie used to always be fooling around with the horn. Yeah. Well, in them days it was cornets. It wasn't trumpets like the...
